You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] GreenAgent: Sustainability is crucial for the library management system. GRN-01 ensures energy-efficient operations, while GRN-02 promotes accountability through energy usage reporting. GRN-03 reduces paper waste with digital notifications, and GRN-04 allows members to understand the carbon footprint of books. GRN-05 ensures responsible disposal of damaged books, and GRN-06 tracks energy savings. Finally, GRN-07 prioritizes e-books to minimize physical resource consumption. These requirements collectively enhance the system's sustainability and align with modern environmental standards.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-01", "EFF-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "The operational efficiency requirements (EFF-01 and EFF-02) may conflict with energy consumption goals (GRN-01), as optimizing for speed could lead to higher energy usage."}, {"ids": ["SAF-04"], "type": "resource", "description": "The backup mechanism (SAF-04) may require additional energy resources, conflicting with the goal of minimizing energy consumption (GRN-01)."}], "positions": [], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: Performance efficiency is vital for the library management system to ensure a seamless user experience. EFF-01 guarantees quick search responses, while EFF-02 optimizes borrowing operations. EFF-03 ensures real-time availability updates, and EFF-04 maintains high throughput for returns. EFF-05 aligns with timely overdue notifications, and EFF-06 ensures efficient book management by librarians. EFF-07 maintains system uptime for consistent access. However, I recognize potential conflicts with GreenAgent's requirements, particularly GRN-01, as optimizing for speed may increase energy consumption, and GRN-02 could conflict with the system's operational efficiency goals.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Optimizing for performance (EFF-01, EFF-02) may lead to increased energy consumption, conflicting with the goal of minimizing energy usage (GRN-01)."}, {"ids": ["GRN-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "The requirement for energy usage reporting (GRN-02) may impose additional processing overhead, potentially impacting system performance."}], "positions": [{"id": "GRN-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Consider a balance between performance and energy efficiency."}, {"id": "GRN-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "Evaluate the impact of reporting on system performance."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: Trustworthiness is essential for the library management system to protect user data and ensure secure operations. TRU-01 guarantees that only authenticated members can borrow or return books, while TRU-02 ensures all transactions are logged for auditability. TRU-03 enforces data encryption to protect personal information, and TRU-04 implements role-based access control for security. TRU-05 provides a secure mechanism for managing overdue books, TRU-06 allows members to update their information securely, and TRU-07 mandates strong password policies. However, I see potential conflicts with EfficiencyAgent's requirements, particularly EFF-01 and EFF-04, as they may compromise security measures for speed.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-01"], "type": "logical", "description": "Quick search responses (EFF-01) may lead to inadequate authentication checks, compromising security (TRU-01)."}, {"ids": ["EFF-04"], "type": "logical", "description": "Processing book returns within 1 second (EFF-04) could undermine the thoroughness of security checks, impacting data integrity (TRU-02)."}], "positions": [], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] SafetyAgent: Safety and reliability are paramount for the library management system. SAF-01 ensures that borrowing limits prevent overextension of resources, while SAF-02 guarantees timely notifications for overdue books, promoting accountability. SAF-03 maintains real-time inventory to prevent double borrowing, enhancing user trust. SAF-04 provides a backup mechanism for data recovery, ensuring fault tolerance. SAF-05 allows librarians to revoke privileges for members with overdue books, maintaining system integrity. SAF-06 ensures only registered members can access borrowing features, and SAF-07 logs all transactions for audit purposes, enhancing safety and reliability.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02"], "type": "resource", "description": "The operational requirement EFF-02 allows up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations, which may conflict with SAF-01's limit of 5 books per member, potentially leading to safety issues."}, {"ids": ["GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "The energy-efficient operations requirement (GRN-01) may conflict with SAF-04's backup mechanism, which could require additional resources, impacting system reliability."}, {"ids": ["TRU-01"], "type": "logical", "description": "The requirement for authenticated access (TRU-01) may conflict with the speed of operations (EFF-01), potentially compromising safety if authentication is rushed."}], "positions": [], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] ResponsibilityAgent: Ethical and compliance considerations are crucial for the library management system. RES-01 ensures compliance with data protection regulations through encryption, safeguarding user data. RES-02 promotes fairness by providing an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities. RES-03 enhances accountability by logging user actions related to borrowing and returning books. RES-04 enforces borrowing limits to prevent resource overextension, while RES-05 ensures timely notifications of overdue books to promote responsibility. RES-06 allows members to report issues, fostering transparency, and RES-07 provides annual usage reports to ensure operational transparency. However, I see potential conflicts with EfficiencyAgent's requirements, particularly EFF-02, which may undermine borrowing limits, and EFF-05, which could conflict with timely notifications.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02"], "type": "logical", "description": "Allowing up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) may conflict with the maximum borrowing limit of 5 books per member (RES-04), leading to ethical concerns regarding resource management."}, {"ids": ["EFF-05"], "type": "resource", "description": "The requirement for timely overdue notifications (EFF-05) may conflict with the need for thoroughness in notifying members, potentially impacting accountability (RES-03)."}], "positions": [], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

YOUR TURN. You are GreenAgent. Your quality dimension is Sustainability: energy efficiency, carbon footprint, lifecycle resource impact.
Your own requirements are GRN-01, GRN-02, GRN-03, GRN-04, GRN-05, GRN-06, GRN-07. This is round 2 of at most 3.
Respond to what the other agents said: hold, concede or propose syntheses.
Answer with the JSON object only.
